Reference / time/duration

time/duration#

Exact immutable durations with nanosecond resolution.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let delay = Duration(value: rat(3, 2), unit: DurationUnit.second);
delay::Span::seconds;          // rat(3, 2)
delay.nanoseconds().string();  // "1500000000"
DurationString(origin: delay).string(); // "3/2s"

Description#

Exact immutable durations with nanosecond resolution.

Every unit is an exact rational number of seconds. A day is exactly 86,400 seconds and is not a civil-calendar day. Negative and zero durations are valid. Construction and scaling reject values that cannot be represented as an integral number of nanoseconds; no rounding is performed.

DurationString is a lossless canonical <rat>s representation. Primitive numbers deliberately have no .duration() or unit conversion methods: a stdlib type is always introduced through its explicit constructor.
